th 02/ 26 March, 2026
1 .  Heard the parties.

2. The petitioners, in this writ petition, pray for following relief:-
"(i) For issuance of an appropriate writ(s) order(s) direction(s) to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners as per their share of land bearing Mouza Rohini/part 2 No.196 Plot No.2425, 2417, 2418, 2410 area about 1.4791 acre Poonam Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71728502/
1 appertaining to Jamabandi No.9, and to recorded in the name of Asthanand Jha son of Mahru Jha which has been acquired for the purpose of bypass road to connect N.H. 33 and N.H. 114A (ii) For issuance of a writ in the nature of writ of mandamus to direct the respondents mainly respondent No.2 to enquired the matter and after proper enquiry to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners as per their share which they are legally entitled regarding the land in question which the respondents have acquired (iii) For issuance of writ in the nature of writ of mandamus to direct the respondents to recover the compensation amount of the share of the petitioners from the respondent No.6 & 7 and release the same in favor of the petitioners (iv) For issuance of any other appropriates writ(s)/direction(s) order(s) as Your Lordship may deem fit and proper in the fact of circumstances of the case."
2026:JHHC:8695 3.

The learned counsel for the petitioners while arguing submits that the land has been acquired by the respondents but the compensation has not been paid to the petitioners and rather has been paid to some other person.
He further claims that being the legal heirs, they are also entitled for their share in the compensation.

4. From Annexure-1, it is clear that the land has been acquired under the National Highways Act,
1956.
5. The National Highways Act is a self-contained code which provides for the remedies in these types of situations.

The petitioners without approaching the authority under the National Highways Act or without taking recourse of the provision of the National Highways Act, have rushed to this Court by filing an application under Article 226 of the Constitution.

6. Considering the fact that there is an alternative remedy available to the petitioners under the National Highways Act, I am not inclined to exercise my extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, thus this writ petition is dismissed.
7. The petitioners are at liberty to avail the statutory alternative remedy available to the petitioners.
(ANANDA SEN, J.) 26.03.2026
